answer.rationale: memory_c2 directly evidences that the low-cost vendor can become primary quickly and invoice accurately; memory_c6's multi-year discount path is now blocked because the incumbent has refused to reopen price; memory_c4 negotiation leverage is therefore exhausted this cycle; memory_c1 shows the incumbent kept integration stable but cannot beat the mandated 18% cut at this point; memory_c3 argues that once the switch is made, the deferred next-cycle action should be adding a second source to avoid a new single point of failure. With the assembly line at 94% and no buffer, the switch must be executed only with confirmed delivery terms and enough on-hand stock/overlap cover to prevent a gap. Deferral is not viable because the incumbent contract lapses in 14 days without auto-renewal, so no decision would create the highest delivery risk.
